These small fixtures retain the selectors and nesting contracts observed on public ATS pages on 2026-10-14. Employer/job content and all candidate values are fictional. No real application was filled or submitted. Scripts in the end-to-end spec are local stand-ins for page event handling, not the vendors' complete applications.

- **Workable:** rendered application at `https://apply.workable.com/credence/j/9AE63CB881/apply/`. First/last/email names, generated file inputs labelled Photo/Resume, screening controls and final native submit.
- **Jobvite:** rendered application at `https://jobs.jobvite.com/reveal/job/ocz0zfw4/apply`. Angular form name and submit expression, autocomplete fields, checkbox groups, and two attachment dialogs appended outside the form. The resume dialog is identified by its own paste label, not numeric position.
- **SmartRecruiters:** OneClick reached from `https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/ServiceNow/744000149338366-software-engineer`. `oc-oneclick-form`, nested open Lit roots, SPL inputs/phone/select/autocomplete, two resume dropzones and Next. Blank experience and education editors were opened and their rendered structure inspected without entering candidate data. `smartrecruiters-entries.html` covers repeatable entry boundaries, role/degree fields, current employment and month-year controls. The adapter opens the first empty editor only; the owner reviews and saves each entry. It does not automate a sequence of saves. `smartrecruiters-screening.html` reconstructs the platform's published text, textarea, radio, checkbox and single/multi autocomplete templates; **a real candidate was not advanced to that step**. `smartrecruiters-sources.json` records the observed/source-only distinction and asset hashes. `template[data-shadow]` is a local fixture encoding hydrated by tests; it is not vendor markup. Job context is read as inert JSON. Employer-specific conditional logic and advanced currency/shift/language/file widgets remain unverified.
- **iCIMS:** public job and email gate at `https://careers-appliedsystems.icims.com/jobs/6419/sales-consultant/job`. After the owner used the email gate, the real **Candidate Profile** page was inspected without editing values. It still displayed **Create a login** and two new-password controls, so it is not counted as authenticated verification. `icims-candidate.html` retains the observed `profileForm`, profile IDs, aria labels/required flags, resume upload, salary components and Next button; `icims-sources.json` records evidence and boundaries. The real dropdown loads a separate list on opening while its native select keeps only the current option. The state placeholder has a nonempty value and must not count as filled. The credential-free test variant is explicitly derived by removing the login block; **it is not an authenticated capture**. Since 2026-10-20 a profile that creates a login is filled but for its login and passwords: a fill report from Rivian's Candidate Profile (`us-careers-rivian.icims.com`) showed the same **Create a login** block above the profile's own fields, and the card had read nothing there. The original `icims.html` remains a smaller reconstruction. Dropdown contracts are also confirmed by public `script/common/icimsDropdown.js`, release `platform_188.2.1.261007-495c1342264-11-pg-0`. [iCIMS candidate guide](https://community.icims.com/articles/Knowledge/Candidate-Guide-to-the-iCIMS-Talent-Platform). The subsequent Candidate Questions evidence is recorded below; further employer customizations remain unverified.

The four adapters cover these specific form contracts, not every tenant or stage. Screening questions use the existing rule/AI planning flow. The extension does not press Next, save entries, create accounts or submit applications. Existing acknowledgement rules may tick a checkbox and mark it for owner review; that behavior was not changed here. No consent was accepted on a real site during this verification. Confirmation detection is conservative and only recognizes explicit success; localized or changed confirmation pages can require a follow-up fixture.

The owner subsequently reached iCIMS **Candidate Questions**. That real page was inspected read-only: `form#questions`, two required native Yes/No selects, and the native submit inputs **Finish Later** / **Submit**. A follow-up inspection of this page found the progress list marking Candidate Profile completed, Candidate Questions **step 2 of 3**, and EEO still ahead. The **Submit** caption alone therefore does not identify final submission. `icims-questions.html` preserves these contracts with fictional option values and no user answers. The adapter recognizes this question-only stage; any button with a later progress step, profile Next and Finish Later opt out of application-attempt detection. When the progress list is absent or identifies this as the last step, the previous final-button detection remains; these last/absent test variants are derived, not real final-stage captures. Other adapters keep their existing submit-event behavior. Authorization answers retain the existing rules and owner-review markers, including the existing US-first policy when several countries are named; this work does not change that jurisdiction policy or delegate qualifications to AI. No answer was selected or submitted on the real page. EEO controls, actual employer final submission and confirmation remain untested. This step distinction also agrees with the [official candidate guide](https://community.icims.com/articles/Knowledge/Candidate-Guide-to-the-iCIMS-Talent-Platform), which puts screening/EEO before completed-application confirmation.

Tests cover host boundaries, iframe sign-in exclusion, a profile's login left to the owner, upload scoping, lazy dropdowns, visible placeholders, required/disabled controls, nested roots, opaque radio values, exact multi-selection and clearing, entry boundaries, month-year input, preserved manual values and no automatic submission. iCIMS candidate URLs return to the public job without query or fragment credentials; copied snapshots remove displayed answers and navigation URLs. Profile contract tests do not establish that an authenticated iCIMS tenant flow works. Existing adapter paths and UI styles are retained.
